comments.text:
Physics is at play here.
1 gallon of fuel have the energy density equivalent to 14000kwh and weight that is order of magnitude smaller than the same amount of energy packed into batteries for the same amount of energy.

The only thing that possibly could maybe work is other more sustainable aviation fuels. Electric flight for large long distance aircrafts meant to fly over 2,5 hours is currently not going to be possible with the current battery technology we have available.

they would need to pack an order of magnitude more energy per kg and using materials that are order of magnitude lighter non of that is in the anywhere near commercial readiness, scale and certified for aviation safety at the moment so the realistic future is sustainable aviation fuels for longer distance flights, for shorter distances under 2,5 hours than with advancements in battery density then in the future propeller driven electric planes may become the standard for short haul flights.
